To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the PL and IL cortices of the rat mPFC are involved in recency judgments and object location memory, 2) the PL cortex is also important for recognition memory for object identity, and 3) the IL cortex may be involved in the processing of object location information.

catecholaminergic depletion in the prelimbic (but not infralimbic) cortex impairs recency discrimination, and catecholaminergically depleting the infralimbic cortex disrupts object location recognition.
the PL and IL cortices are both required for recency judgments, but the IL is also required for judgments based on the location of objects.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role that the mPfc plays in the processing of different aspects of recognition memories.
the neural basis of memory for the recency, location, and identity of objects.
the neurochemical and neuroanatomical basis of recognition memory.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mPFO plays a role in recognition memory, but that the role of the IL and PL cortices in this function may be dissociable.
the catecholaminergic system within the mP FC is important for the recency and spatial components of recognition memory.
catecholamine depletion within the mP FC impairs recency and location recognition memory but does not affect object recognition memory.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mP FC is not required for novel object recognition.

the catecholamine system within the PL is crucial for recency and object location judgments, whereas the catecholaminergic system within the IL is important for the integration of information across these different types of memory.
catecholamine depletion within the mP FC impairs recency judgments, but not object recognition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the medial pre-frontal cortex is not a unitary structure and that different regions within the medial pre-front cortex are involved in different cognitive processes.
the mP FC is a heterogeneous structure and that different aspects of recognition may rely on distinct subregions of this structure.
the mP FC is not a homogeneous structure and that the PL and IL have distinct functions in recognition memory.
